newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore parliament defers decision on opposition.
newsitem.headline: Singapore parliament defers decision on opposition.

text.p: The fate of four leaders of Singapore's main opposition party found in contempt of parliament remained in the balance on Monday as a motion to approve fines against them was adjourned until December 11.

Leader of the House Wong Kan Seng, who moved the motion to approve the parliamentary committee of privileges recommendation, proposed the postponement because Singapore Democratic Party (SDP) members of parliament were absent.
The three SDP MPs are not implicated in the contempt case but Wong said it was important they be in parliament when the motion was put.

The committee recommended in a report on November 22 that parliament fine SDP secretary-general Chee Soon Juan Singapore $25,000 (US$17,900) and that three other SDP leaders get fines ranging from S$5,000 to S$13,000.
The four are not elected MPs.
The maximum punishment for contempt of parliament is a fine of S$50,000 and a jail term.
Chee and the others could also be barred from contesting elections if the case were passed on to a civil court which then found against them and imposed certain penalties.
But if parliament follows the committee recommendations it would leave the four eligible to run in the general election that must be held by April.
Chee is widely expected to contest the next elections.
The committee found Chee had fabricated data and falsified documents presented to a select committee on health and subsequently misled it when challenged over the figures.
The others were found in contempt in relation to the same committee hearings.

Chee told the committee of privileges that a key figure in the dispute was a typing mistake and a result of human error. "I deny the allegation that I have presented false documents to the select committee with the intent to deceive," Chee said.
